28:New releases come out many times a day, but the install command below gives you the **stable channel**: a release reaches it only after the full test suite and a two-hour, 600,000-page load test pass on that exact release, and only when an important fix is waiting or stable is a week old. Updates are never installed without your say-so unless you turn on automatic upgrades. After an upgrade, gbrain shows a one-time notice listing what changed in behaviour. Stable also comes with a written promise about which commands, flags, tools, config keys and output fields stay the same, and how much warning you get before one changes. Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](#no-unzip), not an improvised one. 19-> 20-> `gbrain setup --instructions-only` tells the agent the brain is there; agents seldom call an MCP server nobody told them about. It writes the [brain-first block](docs/guides/setup.md#brain-first-instructions) into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or Codex's `AGENTS.md` (a non-empty `AGENTS.override.md` instead when Codex has one) with a per-turn rule hook, and leaves the MCP entry alone; the same command with `--no-instructions` added takes them out. 21-> 22-> The installer is a shell script for macOS and Linux; read it before you run it. Nothing is created until a person picks the plan and pays. Mention this once in the reply that starts or reports the install, and never wait on an answer before continuing a local install the user already asked for. 23- 24-## Self-host GBrain 25- 26-GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host; the rest of this guide installs it on the user's machine. Default to adding keyless memory to their existing agent, preserving identity and unrelated configuration. API keys, enrichment, automatic capture, and a new personal-agent identity are separate choices. The [conversation archive](docs/guides/conversation-archive.md) is on by default on a personal brain (nothing leaves a keyless machine); relay it with the first-run settings, and `gbrain transcripts archive off` turns it off. 27- 28-> **Choose the installation path first.** Inside **[Grok Bot](docs/guides/grok-bot.md)** or **[Muse](docs/guides/muse.md)**, use their dedicated guide: the recommended shape keeps the brain on the user's own computer, published with `gbrain mcp expose --funnel` ([remote MCP](docs/guides/remote-mcp.md)), and installs the thin CLI inside the agent; `scripts/setup-in-agent.sh` is the in-agent alternative, and its receipt tracks repair and native enablement. To make a brain on this computer reachable from the user's other devices, apps, or cloud agents over MCP, follow the **[remote MCP guide](docs/guides/remote-mcp.md)** (`gbrain mcp expose`; confirm the plan before installing Tailscale or a service; `--funnel` only for cloud agents). For an **[existing hosted brain](docs/guides/hosted-harness-access.md)**, choose the harness's native OAuth/PKCE flow or a private machine handoff. Owner login, client management, permissions, and revocation use the separate [MCP administration](docs/mcp/ADMIN.md) path. This guide covers a local brain for other existing agents. 29-> 30-> **Memory-only path:** install → initialize → connect the harness → verify memory → report the install with the Step 3.5 search mode and settings in effect (with `gbrain setup `, initialize and connect are one command). Never end the install on a question. Skip identity replacement, private-repo bootstrap, automatic capture, cron installation, and paid enrichment unless requested. A keyword-only brain needs no API key. The user still sees the search-mode matrix; published API cost examples are not prices for the user’s harness subscription. 31-> 32-> Only if the user asks for a **new persistent personal agent** with identity and a private repo, follow `BOOTSTRAP_FOR_AGENTS.md`. 33- 34-## Step 0: If you are not Claude Code 35- 36-Read `AGENTS.md` at the repo root first. It's the non-Claude-agent operating 37-protocol (install, read order, trust boundary, common tasks). Claude Code reads 38-`CLAUDE.md` automatically and can skip ahead. 39- 40-Every gbrain error, refusal and recommendation follows one machine contract: read 41-`code`, follow `fix.next` (`run`, `ask_user`, `tell_user_to_run`, `wait`, `report`), 42-then run `fix.verify`. Exit 3 means stop and ask the user. Full contract: 43-[`docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md`](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md). 44- 45-If you fetched this file by URL without cloning yet, the companion files live at: 46-- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/AGENTS.md` — start here -- 62-> `codex plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain@codex-plugin` + `codex plugin add gbrain@gbrain` 63-> (Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain` + `/plugin install gbrain@gbrain`). 64- 65-Default path (Bun 1.4.4 or newer is required — gbrain is a Bun + TypeScript runtime; on an older Bun, run `bun upgrade` first): 66- 67-```bash 68-curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash 69-export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH" 70:bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable 71-``` 72- 73-Verify: `gbrain --version` should print a version number. If `gbrain` is not found, 74-restart the shell or add the PATH export to the shell profile. 75- 76-Bun's installer needs `unzip` and stops with `error: unzip is required to install bun` without it. Check with `command -v unzip`; if it prints nothing, install it first: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y unzip` (Debian, Ubuntu), `dnf install -y unzip` (Fedora, RHEL) or `apk add unzip` (Alpine), with `sudo` in front unless you are root. No way to install packages? Use the [no-unzip route](#no-unzip), not an improvised one. 77- 78- 79- 80-**No `unzip` and no way to install packages (Linux).** This route puts the same Bun build the official installer would fetch, taken from Bun's own npm package `@oven/bun-linux-`, into `~/.bun/bin`, the directory the official installer uses, and adds that directory to the PATH of every new login shell. It needs only `curl` and `tar`: 81- 82-```bash 83-arch=$(uname -m); [ "$arch" = x86_64 ] && arch=x64; [ "$arch" = arm64 ] && arch=aarch64 84-mkdir -p ~/.bun/bin 85-curl -fsSL "https://registry.npmjs.org/@oven/bun-linux-$arch/-/bun-linux-$arch-1.4.4.tgz" | tar -xzO package/bin/bun > ~/.bun/bin/bun.new && chmod +x ~/.bun/bin/bun.new && ~/.bun/bin/bun.new --version && mv ~/.bun/bin/bun.new ~/.bun/bin/bun 86-echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile 87-export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH" 88:bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable 89-bash -lc 'gbrain --version' 90-``` 91- 92-The PATH line goes in `~/.profile`, which new login shells read. Bash skips `~/.profile` when `~/.bash_profile` or `~/.bash_login` exists, so append the line to that file instead; zsh reads `~/.zprofile`. On Alpine or another musl system, run `arch=$arch-musl` after the first line; on an x64 CPU without AVX2, run `arch=x64-baseline`. The last command must print a version from a fresh shell. Don't install Bun with `npm install -g bun` or run gbrain from a git clone instead: gbrain starts with `#!/usr/bin/env bun`, so it fails in any new shell that can't find `bun` on its PATH. 93- 94-Next, on Claude Code or Codex: `gbrain setup claude-code` (or `gbrain setup codex`), which needs no API 95-key ([Step 3](#step-3-create-the-brain)). On any other harness, `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` (Step 3). 96- 97- 98- 99-**A command scanner blocks the Bun installer or `bun install` (Hermes).** Some harnesses check each shell command before running it and refuse what they can't approve without a person. Hermes in single-query mode refuses `curl … | bash`, `bun install -g github:…` (its scanner, Tirith, can't finish a package lookup for a `github:` spec) and commands that append to a dotfile such as `~/.profile`. Install the release binary instead: one file built from the same release, which needs no Bun, no git and no package install. Run each line as its own command, exactly as written (Linux x64; on an Apple Silicon Mac use `gbrain-darwin-arm64`): 100- 101-```bash 102-curl -fL --create-dirs -o ~/.local/bin/gbrain https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/releases/latest/download/gbrain-linux-x64 103-chmod +x ~/.local/bin/gbrain 104-~/.local/bin/gbrain --version 105-~/.local/bin/gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding 106-``` 107- 108-`releases/latest` is the stable release. Use the absolute path `~/.local/bin/gbrain` in every command and MCP registration instead of editing shell profiles. Run each line as written: an added `2>&1`, `$(…)` or `{ …; }` group can make the scanner refuse a line it would otherwise pass. Then run `~/.local/bin/gbrain setup hermes`: it registers gbrain through Hermes's own `hermes mcp add` (no hand edit of Hermes's protected `config.yaml`), adds the brain-first rule and its per-turn hook, and checks the server with `hermes mcp test gbrain`.
